subject: Follow-up: Integration & rate-limits (SDK, auth, retries, idempotency)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Cooper <jane@acme-corp.com>; Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Integration & rate-limits (SDK, auth, retries, idempotency)

Hi Jane / Sam —

Thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on the POC:

Recap (integration areas we discussed)
- SDK setup & auth: short-lived service keys vs. mTLS for your infra; KMS integration for key rotation.
- Routing & model selection: prefer routing by intent/latency/cost policy (we can pin a higher-capacity variant for critical routes).
- Structured output / tool-calling: JSON schema enforcement + function/tool calling for retrieval/DB ops.
- Embeddings & rerankers: batch embeddings for offline indexing + online re-ranking calls (we recommend hybrid: precompute dense + online lightweight rerank).
- Rate limits / quotas / retries: per-route quotas, burst window, 429 handling, exponential backoff + jitter, and idempotency tokens for non-idempotent actions.

Attachments: attaching our quick reference on rate-limits and retry patterns (redwood-rate-limit-guide.pdf).

Open questions for you before the POC:
1) Expected steady-state QPS and peak burst (rough numbers) and estimated tokens per minute/hour.
2) Are you planning server-side or client-side SDK integration first? (we can provide both samples)
3) Any mandatory corporate auth pattern we must support (e.g., SAML/OIDC mTLS/KMS)?
4) Who on your infra team will own network/routing and who will own data security/compliance for the POC?

Proposed next steps
- You share the POC architecture doc and a quick traffic profile (answers to Q1–Q2).
- Markus to give recommended rate-limit headers and retry snippet.
- We’ll draft a short mutual-action plan for the POC and schedule a 30-min tech check.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai
[Attachment: redwood-rate-limit-guide.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Jane Cooper <jane@acme-corp.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 16:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Integration & rate-limits (SDK, auth, retries, idempotency)

Hi Rishi —

Thanks for the clear recap. Attaching our POC architecture (acme-poc-arch.pdf). A few quick answers and questions:

Traffic profile (estimates)
- Steady-state: ~200 RPS across the service (most calls are short generative requests).
- Peak bursts: up to ~800 RPS for short windows (~30s) during batch events.
- Tokens: typical request ~120 tokens; estimate 6–8M tokens/day for initial POC.

Auth:
- We prefer short-lived service tokens backed by our internal KMS. mTLS is optional but we may require it for production.

Questions:
1) For 429 handling, if Redwood returns Retry-After, do you recommend honoring Retry-After exactly or applying client-side capped exponential backoff?
2) For idempotency — what header/key do you prefer? X-Request-ID or Idempotency-Key? Any limits on token length?
3) Can you share a small SDK code snippet showing recommended retry logic + request ID usage?

We’re ready to kick off the POC next week pending a short design review with our infra team.

Thanks,
Jane Cooper
Senior Product Manager, Acme Corp
[Attachment: acme-poc-arch.pdf (application/pdf)]
